rows.description: A young adult reading a report or news item separates stated facts from opinion and asks about source and sample. Tone can mask bias, so double-checking claims is wiser than trusting confident delivery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult in interviews or research uses open questions and follow-ups to learn, avoiding loaded or leading questions. A wise probe stays curious rather than accusatory.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult states expectations as predictions and notes the evidence, such as I expect X because of Y. Humility about limits builds credibility, while unearned certainty invites errors.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult disputes a claim by focusing on evidence, using phrases such as the data suggests otherwise. Attacking the person instead of the claim is a common pitfall that escalates conflict.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: In many cultures people avoid a blunt no and say maybe, we will see or yes, but. A young adult reads tone, delay and lack of follow-up and asks a clear yes or no question.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult learns to spot requests that carry pressure, guilt or threats, such as if you loved me you would. A real request leaves room to say no, and unsafe pressure should be shared with a trusted person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: affection, guilt, trust

rows.description: A young adult requests help from a mentor, friend or counselor by being specific about the need and timeframe. Vague requests such as can you help me with something invite confusion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult leading a team or lab gives clear directions with the reason and expected result. Commanding without explanation may achieve compliance but weaken trust.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult reading warnings about scams, health claims or safety checks the source before acting or sharing. Panic messages that push urgency and secrecy are a warning sign in themselves.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult asks someone to stop teasing, texting or touching by saying stop, clearly and without apology. If the person does not stop, leaving and seeking help from a trusted person or authority is wise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
